newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Oil traders disappointed by Oman term crude price.
newsitem.headline: Oil traders disappointed by Oman term crude price.

text.p: The Oman crude price is expected to come under renewed pressure for July trading after the release of the latest official selling price (OSP), traders said on Tuesday.
The April OSP was cut to $17.53 per barrel, down $1.57 from the March OSP of $19.10, traders said.
That narrowed the Oman/Dubai differential, an indication of the crudes value for spot market trading, by just 10 cents to +90 cents per barrel -- a smaller move than had been expected by the trade.
Traders said they had expected at least a 20 cent narrowing of the differential to improve the prospects of selling Oman into the spot market.
The crude slumped to 22 cents below its OSP in trading for June liftings. Last week the price firmed to 12 cents below the OSP, based on a cargo sold by a European refiner to a U.S. major.
But the latest differential has left traders disappointed, they said.
"The OSP has not responded at all. It's very disappointing," one trader said, referring to expectations the Oman government would seek to support spot market sales.
June trading for all Middle East grades was weak, largely because several cargoes were displaced by a flurry of West African imports.
Traders said the imports would continue to hinder demand for July-lifting Middle East crudes.
"The key is the Brent/Dubai spread. If the Brent/Dubai remains at current levels, then the Middle East grades will be very sick," one trader said of the July market.
But the moderate narrowing of the Dubai/Oman differential would add further pressure to the Oman market, they said.
Abu Dhabi grades came in by a bigger 28 cents against Dubai, raising their chances of finding more demand.
